plan.summary: Twelve 2017-20 Broadway productions with no commercial record, from the owner's Oct 21 ChatGPT Deep Research batch (tracker prompts p26-p28), each figure re-read at its source here: SEC filings for Network, The Ferryman, To Kill a Mockingbird; Broadway News, Deadline, the LA Times, AWN, NYT via WRAL and INTIX Access quotes. Recouped: To Kill a Mockingbird (Windfall, Apr 2019), Network (Easy Winner, Mar 2019), The Boys in the Band and The Lifespan of a Fact (Easy Winner), The Ferryman (Trickle, recouped on its closing day). Reported losses: SpongeBob SquarePants, The Prom. Budget only, outcome TBD: The Cher Show, Be More Chill, Carousel, American Son; Once on This Island gets its reported ~$450K weekly cost. Held for Dots: Forbes-only figures (SpongeBob $800K weekly, Escape to Margaritaville $15M, Burn This $4M; Forbes blocks cloud fetches), The Stage's 'presumed' non-recoupment, the Oklahoma! joint Broadway+tour $8.5M forum lead. Not added: Beetlejuice 2019 (its $21M already sits on beetlejuice-2022, the same production). Old values: none (new entries; core data at 34ca3fd).

entry.recoupedSource: Broadway News (Apr 26, 2019): "'To Kill a Mockingbird' has recouped its entire investment, producer Scott Rudin announced Friday morning." It recouped 19 weeks after its Dec 13, 2018 opening. https://www.broadwaynews.com/to-kill-a-mockingbird-announces-recoupment/
entry.capitalizationSource: Broadway News (Apr 26, 2019): "The play was capitalized for up to $7.5 million, according to documents filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission." Its SEC Form D (Atticus LLC, managing members Scott Rudin and Barry Diller, CIK 0001748292, signed Aug 3, 2018) offered $7,500,000 with $400,000 sold by then. https://www.broadwaynews.com/to-kill-a-mockingbird-announces-recoupment/ https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1748292/000174829218000001/xslFormDX01/primary_doc.xml
entry.notes: Aaron Sorkin's adaptation at the Shubert, starring Jeff Daniels; opened Dec 13, 2018. Recouped its up-to-$7.5 million capitalization in 19 weeks (Apr 2019) and became the top-grossing American play in Broadway history. Orin Wolf replaced Scott Rudin as executive producer before the Oct 2021 reopening; the run ended Jan 16, 2022 and the planned return did not happen. Total profit was never reported.

entry.capitalizationSource: Deadline (Mar 6, 2019) reported a $7.8 million capitalization, recouped in 15 weeks. Its SEC Form D (Network on Broadway LLC, CIK 0001755149, signed Oct 2, 2018) listed a $7,750,000 offering with $5,658,000 sold by then. https://deadline.com/2019/03/network-broadway-recoup-7-million-capitalization-1202570575/ https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1755149/000175514918000001/xslFormDX01/primary_doc.xml
entry.notes: Ivo van Hove's staging of Network with Bryan Cranston at the Belasco (opened Dec 6, 2018; closed Jun 8, 2019). Recouped its $7.8 million capitalization in 15 weeks (Deadline).

entry.recoupedSource: Broadway News (Jul 7, 2019): "'The Ferryman' has recouped its investment on Broadway, the production announced Sunday." It closed the same day. https://www.broadwaynews.com/the-ferryman-announces-recoupment/
entry.capitalizationSource: SEC Form D/A filing (Ferryman Broadway Limited Partnership, CIK 0001733075, signed Dec 11, 2018): $6,700,000 sold of $6,700,000 offered (fully sold). https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1733075/000173307518000002/xslFormDX01/primary_doc.xml
entry.notes: Jez Butterworth's Tony-winning play at the Bernard B. Jacobs (opened Oct 21, 2018). Announced recoupment of its $6.7 million on its closing day, Jul 7, 2019, so little profit beyond break-even.

entry.recoupedSource: Broadway News (Jul 16, 2018): "'The Boys in the Band' has recouped its $3.5 million investment after 11 weeks on Broadway, the show's producers announced Monday." https://www.broadwaynews.com/the-boys-in-the-band-recoups-capitalization/
entry.capitalizationSource: Broadway News (Jul 16, 2018): "'The Boys in the Band' has recouped its $3.5 million investment after 11 weeks on Broadway." https://www.broadwaynews.com/the-boys-in-the-band-recoups-capitalization/
entry.notes: Limited-run revival at the Booth (opened May 31, 2018; closed Aug 11, 2018) produced by David Stone and Ryan Murphy. Recouped its $3.5 million in 11 weeks.

entry.recoupedSource: Broadway News (Dec 20, 2018): "'The Lifespan of a Fact' has recouped its production costs after running on Broadway for three months." https://www.broadwaynews.com/the-lifespan-of-a-fact-recoups-production-costs-in-three-months/
entry.capitalizationSource: Deadline (Jan 14, 2019): "Capitalized at a reported $4.1 million, Lifespan, which recouped its investment last month..." https://deadline.com/2019/01/broadway-box-office-32-million-daniel-radcliffe-lifespan-of-a-fact-network-to-kill-a-mockingbird-1202534984/
entry.notes: Limited 16-week run at Studio 54 (opened Oct 18, 2018; closed Jan 13, 2019) with Daniel Radcliffe, produced by Jeffrey Richards. Recouped its reported $4.1 million in about three months.

entry.recoupedSource: Deadline (Jul 9, 2018): "The musical will close without recouping its reported $18 million capitalization." https://deadline.com/2018/07/broadway-spongebob-squarepants-closing-date-1202422980/
entry.capitalizationSource: Animation World Network (Jul 9, 2018): the show closes "failing to recoup the $18.35 million production capitalization it reported in a Securities and Exchange Commission filing." Deadline rounded it to $18 million. https://www.awn.com/news/spongebob-squarepants-broadway-musical-close
entry.notes: Nickelodeon's musical at the Palace (opened Dec 4, 2017; closed Sep 16, 2018), Tony-nominated for Best Musical. Closed without recouping its $18.35 million capitalization.

entry.recoupedSource: Los Angeles Times (Dec 12, 2020), on the Netflix film: "the stage show did not recoup its investment." https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/movies/story/2020-12-12/the-prom-netflix-broadway-profit-sharing-commentary
entry.capitalizationSource: Broadway News (Jun 19, 2019): "'The Prom' was initially capitalized for up to $13.5 million, according to documents filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission." https://www.broadwaynews.com/the-prom-announces-aug-11-closing-date/
entry.notes: Original musical at the Longacre (opened Nov 15, 2018; closed Aug 11, 2019). Capitalized for up to $13.5 million; the Los Angeles Times reported it did not recoup.

entry.capitalizationSource: Broadway News (Jun 25, 2019): "The musical was capitalized for up to $19 million, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission." https://www.broadwaynews.com/the-cher-show-will-end-its-run-in-august/
entry.notes: Cher bio-musical at the Neil Simon (opened Dec 3, 2018; closed Aug 18, 2019). Capitalized for up to $19 million; no recoupment announced.

entry.capitalizationSource: Broadway News (Jun 20, 2019): "The musical was capitalized for up to $9.5 million, according to documents filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission." https://www.broadwaynews.com/be-more-chill-to-end-run-in-august/
entry.notes: Joe Iconis musical at the Lyceum (opened Mar 10, 2019; closed Aug 11, 2019). Capitalized for up to $9.5 million; no recoupment announced.

entry.capitalizationSource: Broadway News (Aug 7, 2018): "The production was capitalized for $15.25 million, according to filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission." https://www.broadwaynews.com/carousel-to-play-final-performance-on-sept-16/
entry.notes: Revival at the Imperial (opened Apr 12, 2018; closed Sep 16, 2018). Capitalized for $15.25 million (Forbes listed $15 million); no recoupment announced.

entry.capitalizationSource: The New York Times (Oct 2018), via WRAL: Kerry Washington co-produced, "helping to raise the $4.2 million capitalization." https://www.wral.com/archive/17909214/
entry.notes: Christopher Demos-Brown play at the Booth (opened Nov 4, 2018; closed Jan 27, 2019) starring and co-produced by Kerry Washington. Capitalized at $4.2 million; no recoupment announced.

entry.weeklyRunningCostSource: INTIX Access (Dec 3, 2018): "An investor said the production's weekly operating costs are about $450,000, and it will close without making a profit." https://access.intix.org/Full-Article/three-broadway-shows-to-close-as-box-office-sinks-and-long-term-issues-loom
entry.notes: Revival at Circle in the Square (opened Dec 3, 2017; closed Jan 6, 2019), Tony winner for Best Revival. An investor put weekly costs at about $450,000 and said it would close without a profit; no capitalization reported.
